hero.eyebrow: Yard Operating System · digital twin of the yard
hero.title: From gate to dock, your yard running in real time.
hero.lead: GPlanSiS | YARD orchestrates gate, scheduling, weighbridge, spotting and docks in one live control tower — and shows where the plant loses hours before it turns into a queue on the street.
hero.note: Live demo with a simulated food plant

trail.label: of actions with an audit trail

gate.title: The barrier opens on data, not on shouting.
gate.text: LPR, appointment QR and RFID identify the vehicle; license, checklist and fiscal document are checked at screening. The barrier only opens with a PLC permissive and a recorded authorizer.

scale.title: Stable weight captured, immutable ticket.
scale.text: Toledo and Filizola indicators over serial or TCP, gross and tare with a stability window, divergence against the invoice and re-entry anti-fraud.
scale.b2: Manual weighing needs a second factor

yard.title: Every slot knows who is in it — and for how long.
yard.text: Live map with dwell per vehicle, spotting queue ordered by move cost and confirmation by scan at the slot. Cold chain and quarantine are slot types, not spreadsheet notes.
yard.b1: Dwell over target becomes a colored exception
yard.b2: Spotters get the task on their phone
yard.b3: Slots with power for reefer trailers

docks.title: Dock windows with finite capacity, no spreadsheets.
docks.text: Dock Gantt with drag to reschedule, conflicts caught before the drop, carrier portal and timing of docking, start, finish and release.
docks.b1: Priority as a rule, not a favor
docks.b2: Portal for carriers to book themselves
docks.b3: Dock time measured stage by stage

tower.title: AI proposes. Your team decides.
tower.text: Bottlenecks detected with estimated impact, proposals with an expiry and mandatory human approval. ISA-18.2 alarms and 11 KPIs updated live.
tower.b3: Color only when something is wrong (ISA-101)

twin.title: The whole yard on one screen — and in the spotter's pocket.
twin.text: Field integrated over MQTT Sparkplug B and OPC UA, data quality always visible and degraded operation when the network drops. The same yard on the tower wall, the gate tablet and the phone.

problem.title: The yard is where the plant loses hours nobody sees.
problem.p1: Trucks waiting on the street while the gate looks for the invoice.
problem.p2: Idle docks in the morning and queues in the afternoon, because scheduling lives in a spreadsheet.
problem.p3: Weights typed by hand, divergence found only at billing.
problem.p4: Spotters looking for the trailer over the radio.
problem.answer: YARD turns each of these moments into an event with an owner, a deadline and a trail.

security.title: Business rules in the database, not in good will.

db.title: Invariants in PostgreSQL
db.text: Double-booked slot, a vehicle in two places, a closed ticket changed: the database refuses, even over raw SQL.

trail.title: Append-only trail
trail.text: Every event with actor, source and time — typed, device or confirmed AI.

roles.title: Role-based access
roles.text: Who schedules doesn't release, who weighs doesn't approve exceptions. Segregation of duties on every route.

lgpd.title: Privacy (LGPD)

faq.title: The questions from the first meeting.
faq.q1: Do we need to replace scales, cameras or barriers?
faq.a1: No. YARD talks to Toledo and Filizola indicators over serial or TCP, to LPR cameras and to the PLC over OPC UA or MQTT Sparkplug B.
faq.a2: Both. The same application runs in the cloud or on-premise, with the field edge at the plant when the network requires it.
faq.q3: What if the network goes down?
faq.a3: The field switches to degraded operation: data quality is visible and no stale permissive opens a barrier.
faq.q4: Does the AI decide on its own?
faq.a4: No. It proposes with estimated impact and an expiry; it only executes what a person approves — and the database refuses any shortcut.
faq.q5: Can we see it running first?
faq.a5: Yes. The live demo runs a simulated food plant with gate, weighbridge, docks and tower moving. Ask for access.
